strengths.title: On-ball involvement
strengths.note: Heavily involved; the team plays through them.
strengths.coach: You were everywhere. Teammates looked for you because they trust you.

strengths.title: Goal threat
strengths.coach: Found the back of the net. Never gets old, does it?

strengths.title: Match-winning impact
strengths.coach: Man of the Match. The game noticed, and so did I.

weaknesses.detail: Tackles attempted: 2 (bottom quarter of midfielders is 2 or less)
weaknesses.title: Defensive work rate
tips: As a CDM/CM, screen the back line: stay between the ball and our goal and pick off passes.
Get stuck in. A won tackle is worth about 0.2 rating, and even 1 in 8 pays for the attempts.
Track your runner all the way into the box. Most goals against come from late, unmarked runs.
weaknesses.coach: Need more bite without the ball. Defending is everybody's job.

weaknesses.detail: 17/25 passes (68%) - below the ~72% point where extra passes start costing rating
weaknesses.title: Forcing passes
tips: Below about 72% the extra passes start costing us. Pick the simple option until the touch comes back.
Through balls only when the runner is already moving and on the last defender's shoulder.
If nothing's on, keep it: shield, turn back, let the shape reset. Patience is a pass too.
weaknesses.coach: We tried to force a few too many. Not every pass has to be a love letter.

weaknesses.detail: 25 passes but no key passes - plenty of the ball, little going forward
weaknesses.title: Playing forward
tips: Look forward first. Check the striker's run and the gap between the lines before the sideways pass.
Switch play when they shift across. Quickest way to find space is usually on the far side.
Arrive late at the edge of the box for cutbacks. That's where midfield chances come from.
weaknesses.coach: Plenty of the ball, but not much going forward. Let's hurt 'em with it.

coach.opener: Well, BellyTb1, a 8.6 is the kind of night you tell your grandkids about. Top 10% of midfielders, and you earned every bit.

push.title: W 4-2 vs Trotted On | You: 8.6 (2nd best match performance)
push.body:
BellyTb1, you put up an 8.6. That's the kind of number a coach writes down in pen.

DID WELL
+ 25 passes. That's what wanting the ball looks like.
+ A brace against Trotted On, your 2nd straight match scoring. The goal was open and you walked right through the door.
+ Man of the Match, your 2nd for us. Leaders make the hard moments look easy.
+ 0.6 above your average. That's a staircase and you're climbing.
+ Your 2nd best match performance: 8.6. That's the standard now.

WORK ON
- Only 2 tackles attempted. Focus point: As a CDM/CM, screen the back line: stay between the ball and our goal and pick off passes.
- 68% passing (17 of 25). Keep this in your pocket: If nothing's on, keep it: shield, turn back, let the shape reset. Patience is a pass too. Habits beat highlights.
- No key passes from 25 passes. Let's sharpen this: Look for the third man: pass to the feet of the player who can find the runner.
- Team project for you and tuxedo_slide: defensive work rate. The plan: pass runners off and track them into the box.

Repetition station: Track your runner all the way into the box. Most goals against come from late, unmarked runs.

Remember, BellyTb1: The ball is round, the game is long, and you're doing just fine.

That's the kind of night that makes me glad I took this job. - Coach Lasso

weaknesses.title: On-ball involvement
tips: Show for it. Move into the passing lane and ask for the ball instead of hiding behind your marker.
Give the passer an angle - diagonal to the ball, not flat in a line where it can't reach you.
Move after you pass. A pass-and-move player is always an option.

push.title: W 4-2 vs Trotted On | You: 8.4 (worst match performance)
push.body:
An 8.4 from tuxedo_slide, your worst match performance. That's a good night's work.

DID WELL
+ A brace against Trotted On, your 2nd straight match scoring. Goals are like biscuits: always better shared, but I'll take this one.
+ 1 key pass. Selfless as a church potluck, and twice as filling.
+ You & BellyTb1 clicked. That partnership's got more legs than a centipede in a sack race.
+ 3 shots on target earned +0.1. That's interest on hard work.
+ Beat Trotted On 4-2. That's a team that believes.

WORK ON
- 54% passing (6 of 11). Habit to build: Simple and on the ground to the open, facing teammate. Driven and lofted balls are for clear lanes only. That's a promise.
- Only 11 passes. Real quick: Play with your head up between touches. You can't find a pass you never looked for. That's a coach's honest word.
- Only 1 tackle attempted. A little secret: Second-ball awareness: after a header or clearance, be the first one to the loose ball. Trust the work.
- BellyTb1 struggled with defensive work rate too. Work on it as a pair: pass runners off and track them into the box.

Five-minute drill: Scan before the ball gets to you - a quick shoulder check means you already know the pass before you need it.

tuxedo_slide, one more thing before you log off: A good teammate is like a good umbrella. You don't notice 'em till it rains.

Tell your mama I said hi. - Coach Lasso

push.title: W 4-2 vs Trotted On | You: 7.3 (3rd worst match performance)
push.body:
A 7.3, PhogsToffees. Think of it like a first pancake. Next one's gonna be golden.

DID WELL
+ 1 key pass. Making your teammates look good is the most generous thing in football.
+ You and BellyTb1 had more chemistry than a high school lab.
+ Win against Trotted On, 4-2. Somebody cue the music.

WORK ON
- No shots. My two cents: Attack the box. Near post and far post on every cross and every cutback.
- 72% passing (23 of 32). Tell you what: Before the killer ball, check: is my runner onside, moving, and unmarked? Two out of three isn't enough. You'll thank me later.
- forcing passes showed up for you and BellyTb1. Talk it through and give each other short options.
- 0.7 under average. Even good weeks have a rainy day.
- 7.3, your 3rd worst match performance. Learn it, leave it.

Garden drill: Get across your defender at the near post. Most close-range goals come from that first-post run.

Between you and me, PhogsToffees: Pressure is a privilege. It means you're playing for something.

Keep chipping away. - Coach Lasso
